Hard Water Stains on Windows in Texas: Prevention & Removal

Spicewood has some of the hardest water in the country — over 16 grains per gallon in most of the Valley. When your sprinklers, pool, or misting system spray water onto glass and the desert sun bakes it dry, the minerals left behind bond to the glass surface. Left long enough, they don't wipe off — they have to be dissolved or polished off. Here's how it actually works.
What hard water actually does to glass
No pressure — just a real price.
What hard water actually does to glass

Hard water is water carrying dissolved calcium, magnesium, and silica. When the water dries, those minerals are left behind as a chalky film. On glass, the film first sits on the surface. Left in Spicewood sun, it slowly bonds to the silica in the glass itself — a process called etching. Once etched, the stain is physically inside the glass surface and requires a light abrasive polish to remove.
Fresh mineral spots (under 30 days) usually clean off with an acid-based wash. Anything older is likely etched and needs professional polishing.

Bleach — makes the etching worse and damages window frames.
Pressure washers — force water past seals and destroy weatherstripping.
Ammonia-based glass cleaner on hot glass — flashes off and re-deposits minerals.

Adjust sprinkler heads so no spray touches windows or stucco.
Install a whole-house water softener or a hose-bib filter for exterior use.

How to Choose a Window Cleaning Company in Spicewood: A 10-Point Checklist

Spicewood has more window cleaners than most cities because the barrier to entry is low — a truck, a squeegee, and a Facebook ad. That's fine for a $50 pane, but for a full-home clean at $200–$400, you're trusting someone with ladders on your walls, chemicals on your paint, and access to your home. Here's how to pick right.
No pressure — just a real price.
Registered LLC in Texas with a current TX business filing.
Active General Liability insurance ($1M+) — ask for the certificate.
Workers' Compensation coverage — protects you if a crew member is injured on your property.
Dishonesty bond — required for anyone working inside your home.
BBB profile with an A+ rating and long-term history.
Documented deionized-water process for exterior work in hard-water zones.
Written streak-free guarantee — not just verbal.
Matching uniforms and marked vehicles — indicates a real team, not a subcontractor.
Background-checked crews if you have staff, kids, or pets at home.
Transparent pricing — a written quote before the crew arrives, not a 'we'll see when we get there' price.
Door-to-door sales pitch with same-day 'discount' pressure.
Cash-only pricing with no invoice offered.
Vague answers about insurance or bonding.
No physical business address, only a cell phone.
Reviews clustered in a two-week window with generic wording.

A trustworthy Spicewood window cleaner will give you a quote in writing, break out any add-ons (screens, hard-water, solar panels), and not require a deposit for standard residential work. If the number sounds too good — under $100 for a full home — the crew is either uninsured, using tap water on your glass, or planning to upsell on arrival.
'Are you insured, bonded, and a registered Texas LLC?'
'Do you use deionized water on exterior glass?'
'What's the total price, in writing, including screens and tracks?'
